_notes: language: language of the panel and the chat, "es" (default) or "en" (one data/i18n/<code>.json file per language; a missing tag falls back to Spanish); --language overrides it. Card and hero names stay as printed. With --resume the language the game was saved in is used again, unless --language is given explicitly (then lines already saved, such as ability_wait or the applied lines of a combat, may stay in the old language).

ongoing_hold: seconds the bot pings your ONGOING scheme on its zone, after saying why it left play, before moving it to your discard pile itself; 0 skips the pause. If the table cannot do it you are asked to move it by hand.

wildfire_hold: seconds the bot (playing Liz) leaves the bottom card that Wildfire discards in view, face up on its discard pile, before applying its effect; 0 turns it off and applies it at once. The wait happens inside TTS, in the same message.

action_announce_hold: seconds between the chat notice of what the bot is about to do (maneuver, attack, scheme, ability, resolution of its combat) and the writes on the table; 0 turns it off and the notice comes afterwards, as before. In fast mode the wait goes inside the same TTS script (lua.hold). wildfire_hold and ongoing_hold are the same pause for those two scenes, with their own duration.

bot_pause: seconds of pause after each bot action (and before your turn) so the table does not move all at once; 0 turns it off; --bot-pause overrides it. It is a Python sleep: it costs no TTS messages.

bot_hero / human_hero: slug of data/heroes/<slug>.json of each side (medusa, hellboy, abe-sapien, baba-yaga, liz-sherman, leonardo, donatello, michelangelo, raphael or houdini; not the same on both sides: their GUIDs would be the same). "auto" (or the key missing) = the bot detects it at start-up by reading the table: a hero is present if there is a loose Deck or Card with a CardID of its range (data/tts/<slug>.json, deck.card_ids; what is inside bags does not count) AND, for decks, by the deck image identity (deck.identity, see docs/card-identity.md: several heroes share CardID ranges, so the range alone does not tell them apart) and it belongs to the side whose bot_deck_spot / human_deck_spot is closest; if it is unclear, it refuses to start and says so. Priority: --bot-hero / --human-hero > value written here > detection (with --resume, the saved game wins over detection). If the table cannot be read, it falls back to medusa / hellboy with a warning. What this key leaves out, the configuration can override by hand (pieces, dials, nicknames, bot_deck_guid, human_deck_guid, destiny_dial), but with another pair of heroes it is normally better not to write it.

start_spaces: REAL starting spaces of the table (Medusa on 30, Hellboy on 3); they are not those of the default map. bot_discard_bounds: (center x, center z, size x, size z, rotY) of zone 906a7a read from the save (live.json 27/10): the discard grid only uses slots whose center falls inside and, when full, stacks on top starting from the first. panel_position: above the playmats (y 1.0) and the objects (~1.57).
dead_spot: where the bot sets aside its fallen miniatures (one per piece, 1.5 apart in x); it is an estimate, calibrate it live. human_dead_spot is the same for the human's.

Setup: the bot deals its hand, decides on a mulligan (once: the 5 cards back to the deck, shuffled and 5 dealt; house rule or unconfirmed, see the README) and places Medusa and the Harpies according to who goes first; the human places Hellboy and Lobster and presses Ready. The starting spaces come from the rulebook (the first player takes space 1 of the map, the second space 2) unless start_spaces is fixed by hand. mulligan_bot=false turns it off for the bot; mulligan_human=false turns off the human's Mulligan button.

Row of the human's cards that look at the bot's hand (Remove A Painful Memory, Advanced Psychometry, Every Possible Angle): bot_row_spot is the CENTER of the row where the bot lays its cards face up and bot_row_step the (dx, dz) between cards (2.6 in z, cards turned 90 degrees; look_rot_y turns them too). Default [11.5, 2.5, -29.0]: a column in z -20..-38 with 7 cards, to the right of the bot's combat (x 4.9..7.1) and ONGOING boxes, past the -z edge of its discard zone 906a7a (x 10.7..19.3, z -17..18) and before the hero bags (z -40) and the die (2.1, -30); free in the 26/10 save. Start-up warns if it overlaps the panel, a combat/ONGOING box or a discard. The Look at bot's hand panel button still uses look_spot.

Looking at the bot's hand (F16, panel button): look_spot is the CENTER of the row where the bot lays its cards face up (an estimate, calibrate it live: in front of the human's seat, outside the hands, discards and combat zones; start-up warns if it overlaps the panel or a combat box) and look_step the (dx, dz) between cards (2.6 in z for cards turned 90 degrees; up to 12 cards). look_rot_y (optional) turns the cards; default bot_discard_rot_y.

unpack (optional, off): with --unpack or "unpack": true (only the boolean true) the bot, BEFORE playing and never with --resume, takes out of each hero's inner bag whatever is not on the table (no GUID of its states; a deck, in addition, with no Deck or Card of its CardID range anywhere on the table) and lays it in a row from bot_unpack_spot / human_unpack_spot (default [22,2.5,-10] and [-22,2.5,10.5], outside the hand zones; each unpack_step [0,0,3]); the deck goes to its deck spot and is shuffled. If the inner bag is not on the table it does nothing and warns; it never takes from an infinite bag. start_spaces accepts fighter ids or the keys bot / human.

bot_tuck_spot / bot_removed_spot (Donatello, estimates: calibrate live): where the bot lays the inventions it tucks under its hero card and the cards it removes from the game, face up. Defaults [18,1.7,-24] and [18,1.7,-28]: two rows growing in +x (1.6 per card), past the bot_row_spot look column (x up to 13.1), beyond the -z edge of its discard zone (z -17), clear of its combat and ONGOING boxes and of dead_spot (z -20). Start-up warns if either row (6 cards) overlaps the panel, a combat/ONGOING box, a discard, a look row or the other. Without them the bot only says what to move and you move it. The human tucks and sets aside by hand.

card_zoom: when true (default) the bot shows a BIG copy of the card the human must read, like Alt+hover but triggered by it: its combat card when it is revealed (or discarded without a flip), its schemes (glance, frenzy, scheme) as they leave its hand, its ONGOING scheme placed face up and the card Wildfire discards. The copy is spawned in the same TTS message as the write, floats at card_zoom_spot, is locked and not interactable, and destroys itself after card_zoom_seconds; only one at a time. It is a Card with its own CardID (99900+) and the name SparringZoom: no read of the table takes it for a card. --no-card-zoom turns it off for a run. card_zoom_scale is the size factor (4 = four times a card), card_zoom_spot (x, y, z) must stay outside every zone (the default floats 12 above the board centre), card_zoom_rot (optional, x y z degrees) defaults to flat with the same turn as the look row (look_rot_y or bot_discard_rot_y), readable from the human seat; add an x tilt to lean it toward the camera. Estimates: calibrate live.
